edges.description: The compound genotype is associated with reduced myocardial GET3 abundance.
Val163Ala directly impairs insertion in a reconstituted assay, despite preserved substrate capture by the folded fraction.
Reduced availability of a functional targeting factor may compound the insertion defect.
Cardiac Asna1 deletion reduces components of the upstream targeting machinery; the stabilization mechanism remains unresolved.
Impaired membrane insertion is proposed to lower the stability of selected substrates; abundance data alone do not establish the complete route.
Loss of selected trafficking proteins may disturb vesicle transport, but the inference is based mainly on expression measurements.
Altered handling of multiple cardiac membrane proteins is a proposed route to contractile failure; the critical substrates remain uncertain.
Systolic dysfunction and chamber dilation accompany the clinical cardiomyopathy; the feedback between remodeling and contraction is not resolved in the small series.
Reduced pump function culminates in clinical decompensation.
Ventricular dilation with impaired systolic function defines the observed cardiomyopathy.
The pump-failure process manifests clinically as heart failure.
The assay directly separates capture from insertion.
edges.limitations: A purified cross-species protein assay lacks intact cardiomyocyte trafficking and does not measure ATPase activity or patient outcomes.
